name: Independent Work Permit / Self-Employment

value.note: assessed by the International Labour Force Policy Advisory Board on education, experience, contribution to science/technology, economic/employment impact, and capital share if a company partner

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a merit-based assessment by the International Labour Force Policy Advisory Board covering education, professional experience, contribution to science and technology, economic/employment impact, and capital share if applying as a company partner.
requirements.fix_path: Build and document a strong case against the assessment criteria.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Social Security — International Labour Force Law No. 6735, independent work permit provisions

notes: Genuinely distinct from tr_work_permit — no employer sponsorship at all, assessed directly on the applicant's own merit by a dedicated policy advisory board, closer in spirit to a self-petition route than most other work-authorization pathways in this dataset. Foreign company partners applying under this route separately follow the capital/employment thresholds described on tr_work_permit (500,000 TRY paid-in capital, or the $100,000 capital-share exemption) — the two routes share underlying employer-side rules even though this one has no employer sponsor requirement itself.
